title: Let's Play House
subtitle: A delicious biscuit, adorned with snow-like sugar. This half is for you, and the other is for me. My friend... I miss you so much.

items.text: Everything is going smoother than expected.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Laplace has forwarded the Uluru Games application to the Foundation, and it has been moving smoothly in the system in the last two weeks. I heard that from Mr. Slouch Hat on the phone this morning.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: They believe it will be a good opportunity to build a positive image for arcanists, and it will strengthen the communication between them and humans. The Foundation is happy to see that happen.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Then when will we have the result of the application?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The procedure is long and complicated. Besides, the safety reports were only submitted a few days ago, so it will take at least 20 days.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Twenty days? If we start the construction after that, we'll never make it on the opening day. The engineers said the construction will take at least a month and a half.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's almost the fastest they can do. Can we postpone it a bit more?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hmm ... I'm afraid not. I already postponed it until half a month later for the construction. Summer will be over if we wait any longer.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: It's okay. We have talked about the construction arrangement.
A map marked with writings is rolled out on the table. Ezra draws a new line.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: We may start the renovation ourselves, and move on to other things when we have more people to help. As I demonstrated here, if we plan it properly, we may be able to finish the construction in a month.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: By then, we can start the event as Ms. Spathodea first planned.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Gosh! I already checked the schedule a hundred times!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: How did you manage to cut down 15 days from nowhere?! This is unbelievable!
Spathodea holds the paper level to her nose and has a read.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You're a genius, Ezra! I guess the Games would have died on the vine without you!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: It's nothing extraordinary, compared to what a real human genius can do. Don't forget arcanists are the pillar of the Games.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Let me see ... Divide the construction team into three groups, one building the entrance, and the other two repairing the internal ceiling and walls ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: ... The internal ceiling and walls?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ezra, I have never made that request to the construction team. You must be mistaken. We need not repair what's inside the Stadium!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I added it to the list.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I have investigated the site with some workers from the construction team. The Stadium is ancient. The walls are badly weathered and can barely hold up anything. It has become more of a natural scenic spot than a Stadium for sports.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: For safety reasons, we might use a support structure made of alloy to ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: No! Definitely NO!
Spathodea stands up quickly, overturning the chair.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: This is the Uluru Stadium we're talking about, not some office building on the street! I will not let you in!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I wouldn't have left the gate open if you told me your plan earlier!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But what about the audience, Ms. Spathodea? How are we going to look after their safety?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: If one of the walls or the ceiling collapses, how can they escape?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Nothing like that has happened before, not even one case in the past hundreds of years!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Nothing stays the same forever. We have to foresee the danger before it is too late.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: They can run away from the danger themselves.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Excuse me?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You already figured it out, right? The Stadium can get rid of fatigue from arcanists and adjust their conditions and arcane abilities to their best.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Even if accidents really happened, they can protect themselves. The prophets and diviners will also warn the others.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: We never needed metal bars above our heads to protect us!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: What about the human audiences?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: They have no superpower, nor super senses. They can't fly a broom or teleport themselves. They can't even get themselves out of a packed room.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: In your plan, how are you going to ensure their safety?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Humans? What are they doing in the Stadium?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: There has never been a single human in the Uluru Games. None of them managed to find the entrance, not to mention enter it ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But I am human, Ms. Spathodea.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: You invited me to the Games. It's also you who told me that humans, like myself, can enter the Uluru Stadium if it shows itself!
The cup in his hand falls to the table.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You ... I-I thought you were different!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You showed concern about arcanists, and you helped us a lot. You're a kind human ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But I'm not special.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I am no greater than any other humans. I don't deserve to be treated differently. I'm just one of the majority, an ordinary human.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: If I can be accepted by the Stadium, so can other humans!
Ezra presses on the map dotted with red marks, dragging that arc he drew towards himself.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Spathodea, Ezra ... Guys, calm down! This is not the time for a fight!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: This is not the time?! When shall we have it then?!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: The world is full of sports games for humans! One after another and another!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: But THIS, this is the only sports game for arcanists! Why don't you go mind your own games?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: And haven't humans stolen enough from us? They even made our arcane skills accessible to them. They modified arcane gadgets and added some science stuff and ... Bang! The arcane tricks I know suddenly became something new—some invention exclusive for humans' use!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: And now, they're even taking away the Uluru Stadium with metal bars?! It was me who found this Stadium, and I'm not giving it to anyone!
Not to be outdone, the girl pulls the map to her side.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Taking away?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: We, no ... I-I have never thought of taking anything away from you, Ms. Spathodea.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I was just trying to help, like most of the Laplace researchers. We spend most our time in the lab, we read, we study day and night ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: We weren't doing it to make humans noble, nor for arcanists!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Those products and achievements ... They are the fruit of the combination of arcanum and science. They were made to make everyone's life better.
One side is full of sullen resentment.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Make life better? Get out! You think I never saw the ad of Laplace?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: "Guide arcanum with science, tame the orderless power with sense." That's what you tell the people!
The other side seems unwilling and filled with grievance.
Spathodea cranes out to Ezra, her face flushed with anger.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Sense will guide sentiments, so as to prevent the latter from destroying itself in the flames.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: You have to attend to the flames carefully, to understand them, protect them from danger ... This is what I've been taught, and this is also the principle I've always acted upon.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: And this very suitcase that we are staying in is also placed at the entrance made by humans! You shouldn't think so ill of them when you're standing on it!
The rational, delicate boy frowns and grips the pen until his finger whitens.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: We were only trying to help, that's all!
Rip! The drawing is torn into two pieces, underneath which the table in between seems like the King's Canyon.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I'm out! It's pointless arguing with a rude human who has no respect for arcanists!
First trotting, then scooting and running, Spathodea storms toward the room at the end of the hallway. "Bang!" She slams the door and shuts the world out.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Sorry, I will go back to my room now.
Head lowered and murmuring, Ezra runs away from the table as if chased.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's a nice map.
She puts the two pieces together, but the crack on the paper still can't be ignored.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It shouldn't be left in halves. What do you think?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I don't like the idea of giving up, and I have never messed up a job once I took it.
Desert Flannel pushes the left half of the map towards the burning flame.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I'll take care of this, and you look after that. What do ya say?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ulu? Are you alright?

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: I'm fine. I just ... feel a bit dizzy ...

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: My head has been feeling heavy since the battle against the Bunyips, and sometimes even my body feels itchy. I think I'll be fine after I fully recover.
Ulu shakes her head and picks up the broken map.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Leave this half to me. I'll talk to her.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thanks, Ulu. I'll request another raise of your accelerants from Laplace.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Desert Flannel, you take care of Ezra. I'll follow the progress of the Foundation's examination.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Let's move, friends.
The people set out for their targets one after another, leaving only empty chairs in the room.

items.speaker: Bunyip
items.text: Ssss ...
A small figure as black as cinder walks out of one pool of shadow.
And then vanishes into the other.
The Australian Nagger Office

items.speaker: Chief Editor
items.text: What the heck did you say?! What do you mean "no other progress"?!

items.speaker: Chief Editor
items.text: Progress of the Uluru Stadium Renovation. Who the heck will buy our newspaper for this piece of s**t?!
His mustache quivers with every angered breath.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Sorry, Sir.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: We haven't been able to find anything new about the Revival Squad for a long time. They didn't even step out of that suitcase in the last two weeks after we got their names in the papers.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Neither did we hear anything from the sources … Ugh!
A file filled with papers is thrown into Makower's face.

items.speaker: Chief Editor
items.text: I'm not hiring a notorious journalist like you for this boring news!

items.speaker: Chief Editor
items.text: Get out and find more! Some big and breaking news like that REVIVAL SQUAD OF ULURU GAMES IN CITY HALL WITH BUNNY GIRL!
The chief editor storms off, leaving his lion roar lingering in the room.

items.speaker: Bunyip
items.text: Sss ... SSS!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: ... Heh, it's you. Good timing.
The tiny Bunyip swiftly crawls up Makower's leg and winds around his finger. Seconds later, it turns into a spot of ink.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: The Uluru Games on the edge of total disruption, the Revival Squad ... turn against each other! I knew it, a group of monkeys ...!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: This is fun. The chief editor and that chick will both enjoy this.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Heh-heheheheheh ... *coughs* ...
His body keeps trembling, trembling, and trembling, until he can't help but let out uncontrollable laughter.
